svg.title: One-Click Environment Provisioner — full architecture
svg.desc: Two independent triggers feed infrastructure provisioning via Terraform and application deployment via Jenkins. A bootstrap bridge connects Terraform to FluxCD GitOps. Jenkins closes the loop by committing image tags back to the infra-config repo which FluxCD reconciles into EKS. ECR sits between push and pull. Governance is cross-cutting.
svg.text: Terraform → Bootstrap → FluxCD GitOps → Jenkins CI/CD → EKS · GitOps loop closes via infra-config repo

g.text: S3 bucket + DynamoDB lock — shared state, concurrent-apply protection
Multi-AZ · deletion protection · no public IP
RDS creds generated here — never in state file
Jenkins pushes · FluxCD pulls · IRSA auth
Bootstrap bridge — idempotent IaC → GitOps handoff
Checks EKS truly ready · installs FluxCD · points Source Controller at infra-config repo · re-runnable safely

svg.text: Layer 2 — FluxCD GitOps platform (runs inside EKS as HelmReleases)

g.text: infra-config Git repository — single source of truth
All HelmReleases + app image tags live here · every git push = a deployed change

svg.text: Secrets Manager → ESO → Kubernetes Secret → application pod (rotation without redeployment)

g.text: Jenkins — deployed by FluxCD as a HelmRelease inside EKS
Receives git push webhooks · runs as a pod · authenticates to ECR via IRSA · no stored credentials

svg.text: Layer 3 — Jenkins CI/CD pipeline (6 gated stages — any failure stops the pipeline)

g.text: Pull code · set commit SHA tag
Stage ⑥ polls FluxCD HelmRelease status — 5 min timeout
Pipeline FAILS if not healthy · green build = confirmed running in cluster · not just image pushed
Stage ⑥ commits new image tag

svg.text: EKS cluster — application workloads (reconciled continuously from infra-config repo)
Governance, security and observability (cross-cutting across all layers)
